Engagement Description: Engagement measures how much a track grabs the listener’s attention, primarily through rhythmic stability, percussive strength, and predictability.
Happy Description: Happy identifies music with high valence (emotional positivity). It looks for acoustic signals that humans associate with joy, safety, and celebration.
Name: Name
Party Description: Party is heavily influenced by the presence of a steady, synthetic, or highly compressed kick drum and a repetitive rhythmic structure.
Relaxed Description: Relaxed measures the lack of tension and physical calmness in the music.
Sad Description: Sad measures the emotional weight and low valence of a track. It is closely linked to Melancholy and is often the acoustic opposite of Happy.

Tour BPM Widget: This helps you match the "heartbeat" of your session. If the party is in a high-speed chase, turn the dial up to filter for high Beats Per Minute (BPM) tracks to keep the energy high.
Tour Category Slider: Use these to fine-tune your search. If your party is entering a legendary cathedral, crank up the Mysticism and Heroism. The list below will automatically filter for tracks that meet these specific intensity levels.
Tour Directory Tree: This is your music library. Click a folder to load its songs into the table, or click a single file to play it right away. Favorite folders (marked with a star) appear at the top.
Tour Effectslist: These are your layering sounds. Open a directory containing your effects and click an effect to start it. These run independently of your music, allowing you to have a 'Tavern' song playing in the main player while 'Rain' or 'Bonfire' crackle in the background for extra immersion.
Tour Menubar: Everything else lives in this menu: upload and import, playlists, settings and this tour. If you only need the song table during a session, hide everything else for a clean, distraction-free interface.
Tour View Modes: Under View you choose the layout: Simple hides effects, lights and most filters, Player keeps them but folds the mood panel away, and Complex shows everything unfolded. Single widgets can also be switched on or off in the Filter menu.
Tour Presets Widget: Found the perfect mix of sliders, BPM and mood map position? Click Save as Preset and give it a name (like 'Epic Boss' or 'Spooky Cave'). Your presets appear as buttons above the filter, so you can recall the exact settings and change the atmosphere of the whole room in one click. Right-click a preset to remove it.
Tour Russel Widget: This is the heart of the app. Drag the blue dot to find music that matches the current emotional beat of your game. Want something tense for a boss? Drag it toward Angry/Excited. Want a peaceful town theme? Move it toward Happy/Relaxed.
Tour Song Table: This shows the songs that match your filters, with scores, tags and BPM. Double-click a row to play it, click the star to mark a favorite, or drag songs onto a playlist (create one with New Playlist… in the menu). Right-click the headers to choose the columns, and right-click a song for more actions.
Tour Tags Widget: These are one-click filters. Use them to quickly narrow down your library by genre or instrument. For example, toggle Drums and Dark to instantly find percussive combat tracks.
Tour Upload: Add music by dragging mp3 files or whole folders onto this tree. The menu offers the same with Upload songs… and Import from YouTube…; if you copied files into the library folder yourself, choose Rescan Library. Choose Analyze on a folder to let a connected Voxalyzer agent fill in categories, tags and BPM.
Tour Menu Upload: Right-click a folder in the tree and choose Upload songs… (the main menu has the same entry). That opens this dialog:
Tour Menu Import: Right-click a folder in the tree and choose Import from YouTube… to open the import dialog.
Tour Menu Edit: Right-click a song in the table and choose Edit Song… to change its details.
Tour Upload Dialog: Choose the target folder, then drop mp3 files or whole folders into the box, or pick them with the buttons below it. Folder structures are kept.
Tour Import Dialog: Paste the link of a YouTube video or playlist and click Look up. Then choose which videos to import, where to save them, and whether to create a playlist or analyze them afterwards.
Tour Edit Song: Here you correct the title, artist, genres, BPM and tags, write a summary, change the cover or set a light for the song. Everything is stored in the mp3 file itself.
Tour Analyze: Right-click one or several songs (or a folder in the tree) and choose Analyze. The connected Voxalyzer agent estimates categories, tags, genres and BPM and writes them into the files, so you can filter by mood without tagging by hand.
Tour Player: The player bar controls playback: play/pause, previous/next, shuffle, repeat, seek and volume. Songs crossfade and play at a normalized volume (change both with the options button). Shortcuts: Ctrl+P play/pause, Ctrl+N next, Ctrl+B previous.
Tour Lights: Control your WiZ lights here. A song or a single chapter can carry its own light setting, so the room changes together with the music. If the server runs remotely, a light agent on your home network is needed.
Tour Search: Start typing to filter the song table by name.
Tour Tabs: Every folder or playlist you open gets its own tab, so you can jump between scenes quickly.
